function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Below is a quick snapshot of the **next few major U.S. festivals** that are scheduled after **June 22, 2026**.  
(These dates are based on the most recent publicly‑available schedules; always double‑check the official sites for the latest updates.)

| # | Festival | Dates (2026) | Location | Genre / Focus | Approx. Ticket Price | Official Site |
|---|----------|--------------|----------|---------------|----------------------|---------------|
| 1 | **Summerfest** | **July 7–10** | Milwaukee, WI | Multi‑genre (rock, pop, hip‑hop, EDM, country, folk, etc.) | $50–$200 (early‑bird & VIP tiers) | [summerfest.com](https://www.summerfest.com) |
| 2 | **Lollapalooza Chicago** | **August 26–29** | Chicago, IL | Alternative, indie, hip‑hop, electronic, pop | $70–$250 (early‑bird & VIP) | [lollapalooza.com](https://www.lollapalooza.com) |
| 3 | **Burning Man** | **Sept 1–9** | Black Rock Desert, NV | Art, music, community, self‑expression | $350–$500 (early‑bird & VIP) | [burningman.org](https://burningman.org) |
| 4 | **New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival** | **Oct 12–16** | New Orleans, LA | Jazz, blues, R&B, world music | $30–$120 (early‑bird & VIP) | [jazzfest.com](https://www.jazzfest.com) |
| 5 | **Bonnaroo Music & Arts Festival** | **June 14–17** (2026) | Manchester, TN | Rock, indie, hip‑hop, electronic | $150–$300 (early‑bird & VIP) | [bonnaroo.com](https://www.bonnaroo.com) |

### The “Next” Festival After June 22, 2026
- **Summerfest** (Milwaukee, WI) – July 7–10, 2026  
  *Why it’s a great pick:* It’s the world’s largest music festival, featuring 80+ stages and 400+ acts across 4 days. The lineup typically spans every genre, so there’s something for everyone.  
  *Tickets:* Early‑bird starts at $50 (single‑day) and $200 (full‑festival). VIP packages add perks like backstage access, premium viewing areas, and exclusive merchandise.  
  *Weather:* Expect mild to warm temperatures (mid‑70s°F) with a chance of afternoon showers—perfect for outdoor concerts.  

### Quick Tips for Planning
| Tip | Detail |
|-----|--------|
| **Book Early** | Ticket sales for Summerfest usually open in late spring. Early‑bird prices are significantly lower than the regular price. |
| **Accommodation** | Milwaukee has a range of hotels, hostels, and Airbnb options. Book at least 2–3 weeks in advance to lock in better rates. |
| **Transportation** | The festival grounds are well‑served by public transit (METRO). Consider parking passes if you’re driving. |
| **Health & Safety** | Bring a reusable water bottle (water stations are available), sunscreen, and a light rain jacket. Check the festival’s COVID‑19 policy if applicable. |
| **Weather Prep** | July in Milwaukee can be humid. Pack light clothing, a hat, and a light jacket for cooler evenings. |

---

#### Want More Details?
- **Lineup & Stage Schedule** – Check the official site or the festival’s mobile app once the lineup is announced (usually a few weeks before the event).  
- **Travel & Accommodation Packages** – Many travel agencies offer bundled deals that include tickets, lodging, and transportation.  
- **Local Attractions** – Milwaukee offers museums, breweries, and the historic Milwaukee Riverwalk—great to explore before or after the festival.

Let me know if you’d like deeper info on any of these festivals, or if you’re interested in a different type of event (e.g., food festivals, art fairs, etc.). Happy planning!
